name: Five Card Stud
description: Five Card Stud is one of the earliest forms of Stud Poker, emerging in the mid-19th century. Unlike Draw Poker, Five Card Stud is an 'open' game where most of a player's hand is visible to everyone at the table. Each player receives one hidden 'hole' card and four exposed 'up' cards, with betting rounds interspersed between each deal. This creates a high-tension environment where players must calculate their strength against the visible threats in their opponents' hands.

history.origins: Five Card Stud rose to prominence during the American Civil War, evolving from earlier forms of Poker as a way to provide more information and betting opportunities per hand. It was the standard casino Poker variant for decades before being largely supplanted by Seven Card Stud in the mid-20th century.
timeline: 1860s: First recorded play during the American Civil War.
1910s: Becomes a staple of gambling houses in the United States and Europe.
1965: Famously featured as the high-stakes game in the film 'The Cincinnati Kid'.
Present: A rare but respected game in high-stakes card rooms and professional Mixed Game rotations.
history.cultural: Regarded as a 'man's game' in mid-century literature and cinema, symbolizing cold, hard calculation over the luck of the draw.
history.evolution: The game's transition from 5 cards to 7 cards (Seven Card Stud) allowed for more 'improvement' and complexity, which eventually pushed the 5-card version out of mainstream tournament play.

setup.dealing: Cards are dealt one at a time. The first card is face-down, subsequent cards are face-up.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best 5-card poker hand or by being the last player remaining after everyone else folds.
rules.gameplay:
1. 1st Street: Each player gets one card face-down (hole) and one card face-up. Betting round begins with the lowest upcard (Bring-In).
2. 2nd Street: A second upcard is dealt. Betting round begins with the highest visible hand.
3. 3rd Street: A third upcard is dealt. Betting round begins with the highest visible hand.
4. 4th Street: The final upcard is dealt. Final betting round.
5. Showdown: hole cards are revealed.
keyRules: The Bring-In: Unlike blinds, the first bet is forced on the player with the worst visible start (the lowest card).
Street nomenclature: The rounds are often called 'Third Street' (the first 2 cards) through 'Fifth Street' (the final card).

strategy.basic: Fold early. If your hole card and first up-card don't form at least a high pair or a very strong high-card combination, you should rarely see the third card.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Upcard' Check: Always look at EVERY upcard on the table. If you are drawing for a Flush in Hearts, and you see three other Heart cards in your opponents' upcards, your odds of completing your hand are significantly reduced.
strategy.advanced: Representing a Hand: If you have a high upcard (like an Ace or King), you can bet aggressively to represent a 'Pair of Aces'. Opponents must respect the possibility that your hole card matches your visible high card.
tips: If an opponent's visible upcards already beat your entire 5-card potential, fold immediately.
Position matters less than board texture. A player with two visible Kings is the lead, regardless of their seat position.

variations.name: Fifth card face down
variations.description: The fifth card is dealt face down so only three cards are visible in the last betting round; first to act in that round is the same as the previous round.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation described in rules; no engine overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Lowball
variations.description: Lowest hand wins. Ace counts low. First betting round often started by highest card showing (bring-in); subsequent rounds by lowest hand showing. Standard low hand ranking (e.g. ace-to-five or ace-to-six) used at showdown.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation described in rules; no engine overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Five Card Stud High-Low
variations.description: Pot split between highest and lowest hands; declaration (high or low) after final betting; odd chip to high. Often 8-or-better for low.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation described in rules; no engine overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Sökö (California Stud)
variations.description: Same as Five Card Stud except two extra hand ranks below a pair: 4-straight (four consecutive ranks plus odd card) and 4-flush (four of one suit plus odd card). Hand order: high card, pair, 4-straight, 4-flush, two pair, three of a kind, straight, flush, full house, four of a kind, straight flush.
